plan: Represent the session as a plain dict produced by one canonical factory (_initial_session) so begin/abandon resets and the exact four-key shape are guaranteed by construction.
Deep-copy the appointment sequence at construction into {'id','label'} dicts, keeping input order for choices and a set of known ids for O(1) validation.

Route handle() through a type-string guard into per-action methods (_do_begin, _do_confirm_contact, ...), each of which validates every precondition and field type before any mutation, so invalid actions never corrupt accepted data and never raise.

Build every screen through one factory (_make_screen) that attaches fresh copies of appointment choices exactly when the prompt is 'Choose appointment' and empty lists otherwise, enforcing the screen shape in one place.
Compute error-screen and correction prompts from a single _next_prompt() derivation of the next unmet step, so error screens reflect unchanged state and corrections land on the right prompt.

Expose action_source/screen_sink as duck-typed constructor parameters consumed only by run_once(), which checks for both before calling read_action(), then handle(), then display() exactly once and returns the same screen object — making both ports trivially replaceable by standard-library unittest fakes.
mechanisms: Canonical initial-session factory reused for construction, begin, and abandon
Validate-then-mutate per-action dispatch keyed on the action type string
Single screen factory deriving choices from the prompt value
Next-unmet-prompt derivation shared by corrections and error screens
Defensive copying of appointments at construction and per emitted screen
Duck-typed source/sink ports gated by a RuntimeError precondition in run_once
